_comment: Cross-language parity for #2280: how a tenant's routing is RESOLVED from the conf.d root
(_routing_defaults -> the referenced routing profile -> the tenant's _routing, shallow,
then {{tenant}} substitution; _routing_enforced takes no part) and how the ADR-007
domain policies judge its receiver TYPES. The whole tree is read (#2326, see the last lines).
Readers: tests/shared/test_routing_policy_parity.py (Python SSOT, _grar_parse.load_tenant_tree
strict_policies=True + _grar_validate), components/threshold-exporter/app/pkg/routingpolicy/
parity_test.go (the shared Go package), components/threshold-exporter/app/cmd/da-guard/
routing_policy_parity_test.go (da-guard findings) and tenant-api's
internal/handler/routing_policy_parity_test.go (the tenant_api column). Every reader reads
only this matrix, never another reader's source.
expect.<tenant>.targets: the routes that render a receiver, in render order: main route
(ref 'receiver'), overrides[i], routes[i]; type = receiver.type when it is a non-empty
string, else null. null = the tenant has no resolved routing (disabled, or no layer supplies
anything); [] = routing resolved but the main receiver is empty, so nothing renders.
policy: [domain, target ref, constraint] per receiver-type violation, domains in name order;
forbidden_receiver_types and allowed_receiver_types are judged independently.
rejected_routes: the refs of `routes` entries the generator skips (route_entry_matchers), or
['routes'] when `routes` is not a list; da-guard reports each as invalid_route_entry.
values_not_string (#2431): the fields of the resolved routing whose value PyYAML does not read as a
string - routes[i].match.<label>, overrides[i].alertname / metric_group (unquoted yes, 1:30, a date,
~, a !!int tag): the generator's --strict ERROR, da-guard's routing_value_not_string. Every Go reader
reads those values (and the receivers) as PyYAML does (routingpolicy.WithPyYAMLRouting), so targets,
rejected_routes, policy and escalation hold for both languages: a plain `yes` match value is rejected
and `alertname: no` renders nothing, in every reader. A match key that is no label name makes the entry rejected and its value is not judged.
group_by_invalid (#2503): [field, kind] per bad group_by element of the resolved routing - main
group_by[i], overrides[i].group_by[j], routes[i].group_by[j] - as PyYAML reads it: not_string (an
unquoted 8 / on / yes), empty (''), duplicate (a label already listed), wildcard_mixed ('...' beside
other labels); a quoted "8" is a label name (Alertmanager v0.34.1 validates UTF-8 names). The
generator's --strict ERROR, da-guard's routing_group_by_invalid, tenant-api's 400 for a value the PUT
body writes (a routing profile's is not judged there; a batch op cannot write a group_by). A repeated '...' alone is not a duplicate (Alertmanager loads ['...', '...']); python_differs
may carry group_by_invalid for the non-specific `!` tag pyyamlcompat cannot see.
group_by is judged after {{tenant}} substitution in every reader (tenant `alertname`: [alertname, "{{tenant}}"] repeats).
unknown_profile: the referenced routing profile no profile file defines (WARN), else null.
A reference is any non-empty string, trimmed: '   ' references the unknown profile ''.
An allowed_receiver_types list with entries but no string among them allows no receiver type
(Python restricts on the non-empty set); a non-string forbidden entry matches nothing.
tenant_api.put: '403' = PUT of the tenant's own file (files[<tenant>.yaml]) verbatim is refused
with POLICY_VIOLATION; '400' = refused with INVALID_BODY because a receiver the body itself writes
breaks the receiver contract (pkg/receiverspec, #2295) or the body's own _routing carries a values_not_string value (#2431; one from a routing layer is not judged; both checked after the policy, so a
forbidden type stays '403'); 'ok' = allowed. tenant-api reads _domain_policy.yaml and .yml as the
generator does, and judges the body's block over the root platform overlay (Layers.TenantBlock,
#2486), so an overlay _routing / _routing_profile the body does not replace is judged too.
tenant_api.batch: null, or one patch applied
to the tenant's block on disk: verdict 'policy_violation' when the op is refused for domain
policy, 'ok' otherwise; a patch that touches neither _routing_profile nor _routing is never
refused for the routing already on disk, and a batch op is never refused for a values_not_string value on disk (#2431).
platform (per tree): [kind, file, field] of every platform-file finding, file relative to the
conf.d root. routing_defaults_routes_ignored = a `_routing_defaults` carrying `routes`: both
readers drop them before any merge; Python records a blocking WARN (--validate fails),
da-guard an error finding with an empty tenant.
python_differs: null, or the values the Python side produces where the YAML readers disagree
(the Go columns above hold for every Go reader); `reason` says why.
#2291 - the tenant layer is what the route generator reads: the tenant file's _routing /
_routing_profile over the root platform files' tenants.<id> entries for those two keys (each
replaced WHOLE by the tenant file's). Routing in a defaults block (a `defaults:` mapping, or
the whole top level of a defaults file without one) or in a threshold profile (`profiles:`)
is never rendered: targets null, and da-guard reports it as a routing_in_unread_location
platform row, field = the key path in that file. The generator itself reports nothing there,
so the Python reader leaves that kind out of its platform comparison (its targets pin it).
A YAML merge key (`<<:`) in a platform tenants.<id> entry is expanded before the keys are read, as every reader's decoder does (#2291); an explicit key wins, earlier sources first.

#2437/#2438 - the same holds in domain_policies, a domain policy, its constraints and routing_profiles, and at a file's top level (a `<<:` there supplies domain_policies / routing_profiles / _routing_defaults / tenants; an explicit key replaces a merged one whole); an alias key names its anchor's text.
escalation (#2325): the ADR-007 require_critical_escalation verdict. null = no domain policy with
`require_critical_escalation: true` lists the tenant, or it has no resolved routing / main receiver
(nothing is judged). Else {verdict, leaks}: verdict 'violation' = severity=critical alerts reach no
pagerduty receiver (main receiver not pagerduty, and no rendered routes entry matching severity: critical
sends to one) - the generator's strict ERROR, da-guard's critical_escalation_missing, tenant-api's 403;
'compliant' = they do, and leaks lists, in render order (overrides, routes, then 'receiver' = the main
receiver), every non-pagerduty destination that still receives some of them first (#2312: its match ∪
{severity: critical} ∪ {tenant: <id>} is not a superset of an earlier sub-route's match, and its match
names neither a non-critical severity nor another tenant) - the generator's WARN, da-guard's
critical_escalation_leak (Field <ref>.receiver.type), tenant-api's warnings. The value is the same for
every requiring domain that lists the tenant. No row's YAML readers disagree on it, so
python_differs does not carry it.
require_critical_escalation is read as PyYAML reads it (#2325): a PLAIN yes/Yes/YES/on/On/ON is true and
no/No/NO/off/Off/OFF false in every reader (yaml.v3 alone reads them as strings); a quoted "yes" stays a
string, so the constraint is off and the value is a platform row: domain_policy_unusable, field
domain_policies.<domain>.constraints.require_critical_escalation (the generator's --strict non-boolean
line, which names no file; the Python half compares kind and field only).
An explicitly tagged `!!bool` value is read as PyYAML's construct_yaml_bool reads it: value.lower() in
yes/no/true/false/on/off (so `!!bool yEs` is true); a file that carries one is not refused whole, and its
other constraints (forbidden_receiver_types) are enforced alongside it.
#2326 (ADR-017 / ADR-007 amendment 2026-09-28) - the routing plane is hierarchical: tenants at any
depth; _routing_defaults from the root (any root _ file), then from each subdirectory's defaults
carrier on the tenant's path, shallow per top-level key, deeper wins; profiles visible to their
own subtree; a subtree _domain_policy applies to its subtree only (entries naming a tenant outside
it: domain_policy_out_of_scope, not enforced), every level judged additively. Blocking platform
rows (the generator exits 2 before rendering; da-guard reports them as errors):
routing_enforced_below_root, routing_defaults_null_below_root (receiver / overrides null below the
root), routing_profile_duplicate (one name in two files; the first in root-first name order is kept,
the later file is named). duplicate_tenant is recorded but not in blocking_kinds: the generator
refuses it first through #2315 (exit 1), and da-guard stops earlier, exit 2, on the exporter's
DuplicateTenantError; the later file in name order is named. tenant_api is null for these trees:
tenant-api lists tenant files at the conf.d root only.
blocking_kinds (#2326 review): the platform kinds that refuse the whole tree (generator exit 2
in every mode). Python asserts it equals _grar_parse.BLOCKING_TREE_KINDS and Go that
routingpolicy.IsBlocking is true for exactly these among every Problem kind, so the lists cannot
drift. routing_in_unread_location with field `_routing_defaults` is the one row of that kind the
Python reader also reports (a `_` non-carrier file below the root; --validate-blocking there).

#2412 / #2341 - a `_routing_defaults` that is neither a mapping nor null (list, string, number, an unquoted boolean) contributes nothing, at the root and below; it still replaces an earlier root file's `_routing_defaults` WHOLE (root _ files in name order), so the later file decides. It is a platform row, routing_defaults_not_mapping [kind, file, '_routing_defaults']: the generator's blocking `WARN ... skipping` (--strict: ERROR), da-guard's error with an empty tenant.

#2504 - a null key in a routes match (~, null, an empty `? ` key) is no label name: the entry is rejected in every reader, alone or beside a valid label. The generator keeps that key (as None) instead of dropping it as its loader drops null keys elsewhere, so it no longer renders the route on the other labels alone; a critical -> pagerduty route that carries one is no escalation.

enforced_group_by_invalid (#2503, per tree): [file, field, kind] per bad group_by element of the `_routing_enforced` route(s) the generator renders - read from the root `_` files in name order, a later one with `enabled: true` (as PyYAML reads it: `yes` / `on` too) replacing an earlier; judged only with a truthy receiver that the receiver contract accepts (pkg/receiverspec, _grar_merge.build_receiver_config) and a non-empty group_by list, the `{{tenant}}` shape once per routed tenant AFTER substitution. field is `_routing_enforced.group_by[i]`, or `_routing_enforced (<tenant>).group_by[i]` for the `{{tenant}}` shape; file is the root file the enforced block came from. The generator's --strict ERROR (it names no file, so the Python half compares field and kind), da-guard's routing_group_by_invalid with an empty tenant and Field <file>:<field>. The --policy domain allowlist is not applied (load_tenant_tree does not know it).

refused (#2341): null, or why the generator renders NOTHING for the tenant although it is declared - 'invalid_tenant_id' = its id is refused (tenant_ids, below; checked first); 'routing_not_mapping' = its `_routing` (tenant file over the root platform overlay), as PyYAML reads it, is neither a mapping nor a disabling string (disable / disabled / off / false, a YAML string): `slack`, a list, null, an unquoted false / off / no (a YAML boolean; a quoted 'off' disables). targets is then null. The generator's blocking `WARN ... skipping` (--strict: ERROR), da-guard's routing_not_mapping, tenant-api's 400 for a PUT body that writes it.

#2341 - tenant_api.batch verdict '400' = the whole batch request is refused with INVALID_BODY before any write: a `_routing` patch value that is no disabling string (`on`, `slack`, '', a JSON null) - a flat patch cannot write a `_routing` mapping, so a batch re-enables routing with `unset`.

B2 (#2341) - tenant_api.batch may carry `unset` (a list; only '_routing'): the keys the op removes from the tenant's block on disk after its patch is laid over it. Removing `_routing` turns routing back on for a disabled tenant, so the op is judged like one that writes `_routing`: 'policy_violation' when the routing it re-enables breaks the domain policy, 'ok' otherwise.

tenant_ids (#2341 R8, ADR-035): the ids every reader refuses (Python _lib_validation.is_valid_tenant_id, Go routingpolicy.IsValidTenantID) and accepts. The rule is the tenant-config schema's definitions.tenantId, a DNS-1123 label: 1-63 characters of [a-z0-9-], starting and ending with [a-z0-9] - so UPPER, `_`, a leading or trailing `-` and 64 characters are refused. A declared tenant with a refused id makes the generator refuse the WHOLE tree in every mode (ADR-035 D3: rc 1, nothing written); within the tree it renders NOTHING (no route, receiver or inhibit rule): refused 'invalid_tenant_id', targets null - load_tenant_tree's blocking `WARN ... skipping` (--strict: ERROR), da-guard's invalid_tenant_id (Field <file>:tenants.<id>), tenant-api's 400 on a write to that id. schema_search_accepts: ids the schema's `propertyNames` check (Python jsonschema; JSON Schema `pattern` is a SEARCH and Python's `$` matches before a trailing newline) lets through although every decoded-key reader refuses them - the accepted gap ADR-035 D2 names; Python asserts both halves, Go the refusal.

#2341 - a disabling string is decided as _lib_validation.is_disabled decides it: Python str.strip() (U+001C-U+001F are whitespace too) then lower() on the remaining text, which must be ASCII (U+0130 'I with dot' never lowers to 'i'): `"\x1coff"` disables, `"d\u0130sable"` is routing_not_mapping.

#2659 - `domain_policies: null` (`~`, a bare key) in a _domain_policy.yaml is unusable in every reader: the generator's --strict drops the block ("domain policy file could not be used"), da-guard reports domain_policy_unusable (field domain_policies), and tenant-api refuses the file (routingpolicy.DomainPoliciesShapeError, the shape check da-guard applies) - it enforces nothing of it, as before, where it read the block as an empty policy; the difference is on a hot reload, where it now keeps the last good policy (tested in tenant-api, not expressible here).

# _routing_profiles.yaml — Named Routing Configurations (ADR-007)
#
# Define reusable routing profiles that multiple tenants can reference
# via _routing_profile: "<name>" in their tenant YAML.
#
# Merge order: _routing_defaults → routing_profiles[ref] → tenant _routing → _routing_enforced
#
# Naming convention: team-{team}-{region} or domain-{domain}-{tier}
#
# Each profile has the same shape as a tenant's _routing
# (routing-profiles.schema.json $refs tenant-config.schema.json#/definitions/routing).
# The merge is shallow: a key the tenant's _routing sets replaces the
# profile's value wholesale — including `routes` (write `routes: []` to drop
# the profile's routes for one tenant).
#
# `routes` (ADR-007): label-equality sub-routes. Each entry becomes a child of
# the tenant's main route, AFTER the tenant's `overrides`:
#   overrides → routes → the main receiver (first match wins)
# `match` is label: value equality only (no regex, no `continue`); the
# tenant="<id>" matcher stays on the parent route. Timing / group_by not set on
# an entry are inherited from the tenant's main route. Domain policies and the
# --policy webhook allowlist check these receivers too.

routing_profiles:
  # SRE team in APAC region
  team-sre-apac:
    receiver:
      type: slack
      api_url: "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00/B00/sre-apac"
    group_by: [tenant, alertname, severity]
    group_wait: 30s
    group_interval: 5m
    repeat_interval: 4h
    routes:
      # severity="critical" → PagerDuty, re-notify every 15m; other alerts
      # stay on the Slack receiver above.
      - match: { severity: critical }
        receiver:
          type: pagerduty
          service_key: "sre-apac-critical-key"
        repeat_interval: 15m

  # Global DBA team
  team-dba-global:
    receiver:
      type: webhook
      url: "https://alerting.internal/dba-global"
    group_by: [tenant, alertname, db_type]
    group_wait: 1m
    group_interval: 10m
    repeat_interval: 8h

  # Finance domain — strict compliance
  domain-finance-tier1:
    receiver:
      type: pagerduty
      service_key: "finance-tier1-key"
    group_by: [tenant, alertname, severity]
    group_wait: 30s
    group_interval: 5m
    repeat_interval: 1h
